pairs: Omnis sapientia a Domino Deo est:
All wisdom is from the Lord God,
and has always been with him,
Who has numbered the sand of the sea,
and the drops of the rain,
and the days of the world?
Who has measured the height of heaven,
and the breadth of the earth,
and the depth of the abyss?
Who has examined the wisdom of God,
Wisdom was created before all things,
and the understanding of prudence is before all time.
Fons sapientiæ verbum Dei in excelsis,
The Word of God on high is the source of wisdom,
To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed,
and who has recognized her astuteness?
disciplina sapientiæ cui revelata est et manifestata?
To whom has the discipline of wisdom been revealed and made manifest?
et multiplicationem ingressus illius quis intellexit?
And who has understood the multiplicity of her steps?
The most high omnipotent Creator is One,
and he is the mighty King,
et rex potens et metuendus nimis,
and he is exceedingly to be feared,
and he is the sovereign God.
Ipse creavit illam in Spiritu Sancto,
He created wisdom through the Holy Spirit,
et effudit illam super omnia opera sua,
And he poured her over all his works,
to the extent of his favor,
and he has offered her to those who love him.
The fear of the Lord is glory,
The fear of the Lord will delight the heart,
Timenti Dominum bene erit in extremis,
It will be well, in the very end, for him who fears the Lord,
et in die defunctionis suæ benedicetur.
and on the day that he passes away, he will be blessed.
The love of God is honorable wisdom.
quibus autem apparuerit in visu diligunt eam in visione,
And those to whom she will appear for their consideration love her because of what they see
and know of her great works.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom,
et cum fidelibus in vulva concreatus est:
and was created with the faithful in the womb,
et cum justis et fidelibus agnoscitur.
and is known by the just and the faithful.
The fear of the Lord is the sanctity of knowledge.
Sanctity will guard and justify the heart,
and will bestow happiness and joy.
It will be well with him who fears the Lord,
et in diebus consummationis illius benedicetur.
and at the consummation of his days, he will be blessed.
To fear God is the fullness of wisdom,
and it is a fullness from its fruits.
Omnem domum illius implebit a generationibus,
She will fill her entire house from her offspring,
The fear of the Lord is the crown of wisdom,
And the fear of the Lord has seen
but both are gifts of God.
Scientiam et intellectum prudentiæ sapientia compartietur,
Wisdom will distribute knowledge and an understanding of prudence;
and she lifts up the glory of those who hold to her.
The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord,
In the treasures of wisdom is understanding and the sanctity of knowledge.
The fear of the Lord expels sin.
nam qui sine timore est non poterit justificari:
For he who is without fear is not able to be justified.
iracundia enim animositatis illius subversio illius est.
For the disposition of his spirit is his undoing.
Those who are patient will suffer for a brief time,
Bonus sensus usque in tempus abscondet verba illius,
A noble mind will hide his words for a brief time,
et labia multorum enarrabunt sensum illius.
and then the lips of many will declare his understanding.
Among the treasures of wisdom is the outward sign of discipline.
But to those who sin, the worship of God is an abomination.
and then God will offer her to you.
Sapientia enim et disciplina timor Domini:
For the fear of the Lord is wisdom
And what pleases him is faith and meekness.
And so shall he complete his treasures.
You should not be incredulous to the fear of the Lord.
et ne accesseris ad illum duplici corde.
And you should not draw close to him with a duplicitous heart.
Ne fueris hypocrita in conspectu hominum,
You should not be a hypocrite in the sight of men.
et non scandalizeris in labiis tuis.
And you should not scandalize with your lips.
and bring dishonor to your soul.
And then God may uncover your secrets,
et in medio synagogæ elidat te:
and he may cast you down forcefully in the midst of the congregation.
For you drew near to the Lord wickedly,
et cor tuum plenum est dolo et fallacia.
and your heart was filled with deceit and falseness.
